subject: digital-logic
subtopics: the combinational definition: output is a function of the present inputs only, no memory and no feedback
the design procedure: specification, truth table, minimisation, gate realisation and costing
the half adder: sum XOR, carry AND, and why it cannot take a carry-in
the full adder: sum as three-input XOR, carry as the majority, and the two-half-adders-plus-OR construction
the ripple-carry adder: cascading full adders and counting them for an n-bit word
the carry chain as the critical path, with the per-stage carry delay and the total delay model
the carry look-ahead adder: generate and propagate, the expanded carries, the gate count and the delay
the adder-subtractor: the conditional inverter, the control line on the carry-in, and the borrow and overflow flags
the multiplexer: 2^n inputs and n select lines, the output equation, and the Shannon-expansion reading
implementing a Boolean function on a multiplexer: the two-row table, 0/1/X/X', and the minimum size with one inverter
multiplexer trees: 2^n - 1 two-to-one blocks, the level order of the select bits, and reading a tree back to a function
the decoder: one-hot outputs as minterms, the enable input, and implementing functions with OR gates
the encoder and the priority encoder, including multi-active inputs and cascading through enable and group-select
the magnitude comparator: bit equality by XNOR, word equality, and the most-significant-difference rule
the ROM as a look-up table and its size, and the PLA and PAL as programmable sum-of-products planes
the parity generator and checker: the XOR tree, even against odd parity, and what parity cannot detect
hazards: static-1 and static-0 glitches, the consensus term that covers them, and dynamic hazards

chosen.title: Lecture 16 - Multiplexer: Part I
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: the 2-to-1 multiplexer derived from a truth table
the steering definition: one of many inputs to one output under a control input
a 4-to-1 multiplexer built from three 2-to-1 multiplexers
Shannon's expansion and its if-then-else reading of the multiplexer
the closing summary: n control inputs select up to 2^n data inputs, and higher-order multiplexers come from lower-order ones by cascading
chosen.why: Read from its opening to its closing summary, which is rare in this repository's source history, and it is the only source this run that derives the multiplexer from a truth table and then names Shannon's expansion as the reason a multiplexer can compute a function. Both of the multiplexer cards - the basics and the tree - rest on it, and its closing summary states the 2^n data-input rule and the cascading rule in the lecturer's own words.

chosen.title: Lecture 19 - Decoder with BCD Input and Encoder
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: the BCD-to-decimal decoder and its active-low outputs
the six unused BCD codes as don't cares
the encoder as the inverse of the decoder
the priority encoder when more than one input is active
IC 74148 and the cascade of an 8-to-3 into a 16-to-4 encoder through enable and group-select
chosen.why: The only readable source this run that treats the encoder at all, and the only one that states the priority rule and the 74148 cascade. It also supplies the active-low decoder convention that the decoder card's trap turns on. Read from its opening through the BCD decoder and again at its closing summary; the LED-driver middle section is not quoted.

chosen.title: Lecture 23 - Arithmetic Building Blocks I
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: why a half adder is 'half': it has no carry-in
the half adder truth table and the equations S = A XOR B and C = AB
the full adder truth table and Cout = AB + ACin + BCin, with the sum as a three-input XOR
the full adder from two half adders and one OR gate
the closing summary: ripple-carry connection, and subtraction by the two's complement with a NOT bank and a carry-in of 1, or a full adder plus an XOR bank for both operations
chosen.why: The clearest readable derivation of the two adder blocks in the lecturer's own order, and its closing summary states both the ripple-carry connection and the adder-subtractor construction, which is what the adder, ripple-carry and adder-subtractor cards need. The served transcript stops before the worked ripple and subtractor examples, so those numbers are recomputed here instead of quoted.

chosen.title: Lecture 15 - Static 0 Hazard and Dynamic Hazard
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: static-1 hazard recalled as the A + A' reduction
static-0 hazard as the A.A' reduction in a POS realisation
detection on the map or in the expression
covering by an added sum term
the dynamic hazard as more than one transition, needing three or more levels
chosen.why: Read in full, and it is the only source this run that distinguishes the two static hazards by their reduced expressions and states the three-level condition for a dynamic hazard. The hazards card rests on it alone, which is why that card claims no more than the lecture states.

chosen.title: Digital Logic subject notes, the combinational-circuit sections
chosen.channel: GATE Overflow, subject page for Digital Logic
covers: the combinational definition and the four design steps
half adder, full adder, ripple carry and the carry look-ahead expansions with the n(n+1)/2 and n gate counts
the decoder as a minterm generator and its use for implementing functions
the multiplexer equation and the sizing rules
the paper-by-paper mark distribution, used to check which years asked this topic

chosen.title: बहुसंकेतक (Multiplexer)

standard_refs: M. Morris Mano and Michael D. Ciletti, Digital Design, chapter 4 (combinational logic: analysis and design procedure, half and full adders, subtractors, the magnitude comparator, decoders, encoders, multiplexers, parity, ROM and PLA) - the reference the NPTEL Digital Electronic Circuits course itself follows
Thomas L. Floyd, Digital Fundamentals, the combinational logic chapters
GATE 2027 CS syllabus, Digital Logic line 'design of combinational and sequential circuits'
Official GATE CSE papers and answer keys for the years of the recorded PYQs - not fetched this run, which is why every PYQ here is SOURCED rather than key-verified
notes: The syllabus names this topic in five words, 'design of combinational and sequential circuits', so the seventeen subtopics above are this run's enumeration from the standard treatment (Mano chapter 4), the NPTEL lecture order (15, 16, 18, 19, 23, 26) and the GATE question record - not a quotation from the syllabus. The sequential half of the line belongs to the next topic and is not carded here.

Thirteen GATE CSE previous-year questions were verified, from 1996 to 2026, and every one is SOURCED against an accepted answer rather than key-verified against an official paper, so no marks field is recorded and every question reference follows the GATE Overflow numbering.

Two records state a disagreement rather than resolving it: GATE CSE 2004 Q.62, where the accepted answer is 6 time units and some solutions argue 4, and GATE CSE 2015 Set 2 Q.48, where the accepted answer is 19.2 microseconds and the carry-only critical path gives 12. In both cases the accepted answer is reported and the alternative is named.

GATE CSE 2026 Set 2 Q.49 is recorded with the wiring taken from its accepted solution, because the question itself is a figure. The count of 6 is recomputed from the function that solution states, and the record says so instead of implying the figure was read.

Five cards carry no PYQ of their own because no verified CSE question in this topic is decided by them alone: the adder-subtractor, the encoder, the comparator, the ROM and PLA sizing rule beyond 1996, and the hazards. Each card says this in its source line rather than borrowing a question that does not test it.

Only one non-English source was readable this run: the Hindi Wikipedia article on the multiplexer, translated, contributing terminology and no number. No Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture transcript on this topic could be read.

No video transcript was readable: every YouTube route returned no caption track, so videoRefs is empty on all fourteen cards and the four NPTEL lectures are used through their published transcript PDFs, which are text and not captions. That is a gap, not a claim.

The visual lesson animates GATE CSE 2014 Set 1 Q.45: the multiplexer's data inputs, the four select terms, the four minterms and the minimal sum of products. Its cells, minterms and literal counts are recomputed in scripts/validate.py.
